overview: This Senate resolution supports naming July 2026 "National Sarcoma Awareness Month." Sarcoma is a rare cancer of the bones or connective tissues, such as muscles, nerves, fat, and blood vessels, that can appear almost anywhere in the body and has more than 100 subtypes. The resolution notes that sarcoma makes up a small share of adult cancers but a much larger share of childhood cancers, and that it is often misdiagnosed. Its aim is to raise awareness and encourage people to get properly diagnosed and treated. It is symbolic and does not create any program or spending. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on June 9, 2026.
for: Supporters say greater awareness of a rare, often misdiagnosed cancer can help patients get diagnosed and treated sooner.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide money for sarcoma research or care.
